modality.text: Botanical drug product (topical ointment) — an extract of dried green tea leaves (kunecatechins, a mixture of catechins).

citations.quote: In this application, the Sponsor is seeking approval of Veregen, a botanical drug product, for the proposed indication of the treatment of external genital and perianal warts (*condyloma acuminata*) in male and female adults. The product is to be applied topically three times daily. Veregen contains an extract of dried green tea leaves.
This is the first botanical drug product approved in the United States since issuance of the Botanical Guidance.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions are local/application-site skin reactions: erythema (70% vs 32% vehicle), pruritus (69% vs 45%), burning (67% vs 31%), pain/discomfort (56% vs 14%), and erosion/ulceration (49% vs 10%). Local adverse events led to discontinuation or dose interruption in 5% (19/397); serious local adverse events of pain and inflammation occurred in two subjects (0.5%).

summary.text: Veregen was approved October 31, 2006 under a standard review NDA submitted under section 505(b)(1); it was the first botanical drug product approved in the United States since issuance of the Botanical Guidance.
